# Background

Sickle cell disease can cause pain and other complications when sickled red blood cells obstruct blood flow, and exposure to air pollution may aggravate these events. This report cleans daily air-quality measurements from the EPA monitor at RDU Airport for 2018 through April 2020 and summarizes patterns in carbon monoxide (CO), fine particulate matter (PM2.5), and ozone (O3).

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(flextable)

pollutant_colors <- c(
  "CO" = "#0072B2",
  "O3" = "#D55E00"
)
year_colors <- c(
  "2018" = "#0072B2",
  "2019" = "#E69F00",
  "2020" = "#009E73"
)
```

# Data processing

```{r}
#| label: process-function
# process_air_quality()
# Purpose: Read and clean one year of daily air-quality measurements.
# Arguments:
#   file_path: Path to a CSV file containing one year of EPA measurements.
#   o3_units: Desired ozone units, either "ppm" (default) or "ppb".
# Returns: A tibble with one row per date and cleaned CO, PM2.5, and O3 values.
process_air_quality <- function(file_path, o3_units = c("ppm", "ppb")) {
  o3_units <- match.arg(o3_units)

  clean_data <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    transmute(
      date = mdy(.data[["Date"]]),
      co = as.numeric(.data[["Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration"]]),
      pm25 = as.numeric(.data[["Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration"]]),
      o3 = as.numeric(.data[["Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration"]])
    ) |>
    distinct()

  # Correct impossible negative concentrations before computing daily averages.
  pollutants <- c("co", "pm25", "o3")
  for (pollutant in pollutants) {
    negative_value <- !is.na(clean_data[[pollutant]]) &
      clean_data[[pollutant]] < 0
    clean_data[[pollutant]][negative_value] <- 0
  }

  clean_data <- clean_data |>
    group_by(date) |>
    summarise(
      across(
        all_of(pollutants),
        ~ if (all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(date)

  if (o3_units == "ppb") {
    clean_data <- clean_data |>
      mutate(o3 = o3 * 1000)
  }

  clean_data
}
```

Exact duplicate rows are removed before averaging so that repeated records do not receive extra weight. Negative measurement errors are then set to zero before daily means are calculated, ensuring the corrected values contribute to the averages.

```{r}
#| label: combine-years
air_quality <- bind_rows(
  process_air_quality("data/AQ_2018.csv") |> mutate(year = 2018L),
  process_air_quality("data/AQ_2019.csv") |> mutate(year = 2019L),
  process_air_quality("data/AQ_2020.csv") |> mutate(year = 2020L)
) |>
  select(date, year, co, pm25, o3)
```

# Tables

```{r}
#| label: range-table-function
# yearly_range_table()
# Purpose: Create a formatted table of daily pollutant ranges for one year.
# Arguments:
#   data: Processed air-quality data returned by process_air_quality().
#   selected_year: The calendar year to summarize.
# Returns: A flextable containing pollutant labels, units, minima, and maxima.
yearly_range_table <- function(data, selected_year) {
  ranges <- data |>
    filter(year == selected_year) |>
    summarise(
      across(
        c(co, pm25, o3),
        list(
          Minimum = ~ if (all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
          Maximum = ~ if (all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
      )
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(
      everything(),
      names_to = c("pollutant", "statistic"),
      names_pattern = "(.*)_(Minimum|Maximum)"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      Pollutant = recode(
        pollutant,
        co = "CO (ppm)",
        pm25 = "PM2.5 (µg/m³)",
        o3 = "O3 (ppm)"
      ),
      Pollutant = factor(
        Pollutant,
        levels = c("CO (ppm)", "PM2.5 (µg/m³)", "O3 (ppm)")
      )
    ) |>
    select(Pollutant, statistic, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = statistic, values_from = value) |>
    arrange(Pollutant)

  flextable(ranges) |>
    colformat_double(
      j = c("Minimum", "Maximum"), digits = 3, na_str = "—"
    ) |>
    set_header_labels(Pollutant = "Pollutant (units)") |>
    theme_booktabs() |>
    align(j = c("Minimum", "Maximum"), align = "right", part = "all") |>
    set_table_properties(
      opts_word = list(
        split = FALSE,
        keep_with_next = TRUE,
        repeat_headers = TRUE
      )
    ) |>
    autofit()
}
```

### Daily pollutant concentration ranges 2018

```{r}
#| label: table-2018
yearly_range_table(air_quality, 2018)
```

# Plots

## CO and O3 by month

```{r}
#| label: fig-co-o3
#| fig-cap: "Monthly mean daily CO and O3 concentrations with 95% confidence intervals, pooled across available years."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7
monthly_summary <- air_quality |>
  select(date, co, o3) |>
  pivot_longer(c(co, o3), names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month(date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
      levels = month.abb
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(month, pollutant) |>
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(value)),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    se = sd / sqrt(n),
    lower = mean - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean + 1.96 * se,
    pollutant_label = recode(
      pollutant, co = "CO (ppm)", o3 = "O3 (ppm)"
    ),
    color_group = recode(pollutant, co = "CO", o3 = "O3")
  )

ggplot(
  monthly_summary,
  aes(x = month, y = mean, color = color_group, group = color_group)
) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.16, linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ pollutant_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pollutant_colors, name = "Pollutant") +
  labs(
    title = "CO and ozone follow opposing seasonal patterns",
    subtitle = "Daily values pooled by calendar month across 2018–2020",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Monthly mean daily concentration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

Separate panels with independent y-axis scales make both seasonal patterns readable without implying a conversion between CO and O3. Consistent blue and orange colors distinguish the pollutants while the panel labels retain their respective units.

## PM2.5 by month and year

```{r}
#| label: fig-pm25
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of daily PM2.5 concentrations by month and year. The 2020 data end in April."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.8
pm25_plot_data <- air_quality |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month(date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
      levels = month.abb
    ),
    year = factor(year)
  )

ggplot(
  pm25_plot_data,
  aes(x = month, y = pm25, fill = year, color = year)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.78),
    width = 0.64,
    alpha = 0.42,
    outlier.size = 1,
    linewidth = 0.55,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = year_colors, name = "Year") +
  scale_color_manual(values = year_colors, name = "Year") +
  labs(
    title = "Daily PM2.5 distributions vary across months and years",
    subtitle = "EPA measurements at the RDU Airport monitor",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Daily mean PM2.5 (µg/m³)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

Side-by-side boxplots show the center, spread, and unusual daily values for each month and year without obscuring the data with hundreds of overlapping points.

# Interpretation

CO is generally highest in late fall and winter and lowest in late spring and summer, while O3 rises through spring and peaks in the warmer months before declining in fall. PM2.5 shows a less consistent seasonal pattern: 2018 is relatively high in summer and at year-end, whereas 2019 is higher early in the year, and the tables also show an unusually high 2020 maximum of 31.200 µg/m³. Comparisons involving 2020 should be cautious because that year includes only January through April, while May through December are based solely on 2018 and 2019.
